key_insight: Indoor photovoltaics, energy storage, and low-power (anti)ferroelectric computing can be co-designed to enable reliable edge AI without relying on centralized data centers.
engineering_relevance: The paper frames a practical pathway for distributed intelligence by matching local energy harvesting and storage to the power needs of neuromorphic or in-memory computation.
method: Assess the energy requirements of edge/distributed intelligence against available local power supplies.
Evaluate emerging indoor photovoltaic materials for harvesting ambient indoor light efficiently.
Argue that (anti)ferroelectrics can address both electrostatic energy storage and low-power neuromorphic computing bottlenecks.
evidence_signal: This is a perspective article that synthesizes current material trends and system requirements rather than reporting new experimental benchmarks in the abstract.
watch_item: A key implementation concern is whether real indoor light levels, storage losses, and device reliability can jointly meet the sustained power demands of practical distributed AI nodes.
paper_title: Computing at the Edge Enabled by Indoor Photovoltaics and Ferroelectrics
